title: Investing via RBI Retail Direct: Understanding UPI MDR Changes
description: The Reserve Bank of India's Retail Direct platform allows individuals to directly invest in government securities (G-Secs) using UPI. Merchant Discount Rate (.

faq.q: What is RBI Retail Direct Scheme?
faq.a: The RBI Retail Direct Scheme allows individual investors to directly buy and sell government securities (G-Secs), including central government bonds, state development loans, and Treasury Bills, through an online portal.
UPI MDR (Merchant Discount Rate) is a fee paid by merchants to banks for processing digital payments made via UPI. It's a percentage of the transaction value.

faq.q: Why are UPI MDR rules changing for capital markets from October 15th?
faq.a: The government and payment bodies periodically review and revise MDR policies to ensure the sustainability of the digital payment ecosystem, especially for specific transaction categories like those in capital markets.

faq.q: Will I definitely have to pay MDR for my RBI Retail Direct investments?
faq.a: Not necessarily. While new rules for capital market UPI MDR are coming, it's yet to be definitively clarified who will bear this cost for RBI Retail Direct transactions – it could be the investor, the RBI, or another entity.

faq.q: How can I check for any new charges on my G-Sec investments?
faq.a: Always review the transaction summary or payment details provided on the RBI Retail Direct portal before confirming your investment. Official announcements from RBI or NPCI will also provide clarity.
